newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Feb 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- AVIS FLOAT WILL BUY OUT US STAKE

When Avis Europe, the car rental company, refloats on the stock market next month it will buy out its majority shareholders, General Motors and Avis of America. The company is raising 250 million stg in an offer expected to value it at 700 million stg. Alan Cathcart intends to remain both chairman and chief executive of Avis Europe, despite corporate governance codes. The company will have seven new executive directors. The company presently operates out of 96 countries and the new deal will add 27, including China and India.
-- BID TALKS BOOSTS CENTRICA

Shares in Centrica, the trading and service operation being hived off by British Gas, have been helped by bid speculation and a revaluation of its prospects. The business is now valued at around three billion stg. However, Centrica has warned it will not pay dividends in the short term and still faces tough negotiations to end its North Sea contract problems and analysts say tany bid would involve a considerable gamble.
-- AIRPORT CONTRACT BRINGS THREAT OF TUNNEL PROTEST

Tarmac and Amec have been awarded a 100 million stg contract to build a second runway at Manchester Airport, which could lead to one of the next big environmental protests. The Green Party is seeking a judicial review of the government decision to let the development go ahead. The runway will be the first built in Britain in 20 years and is designed to help the airport cope with 30 million passengers a year, double current levels, and bigger aircraft.
THE TIMES
-- NATIONAL EXPRESS AWARDED SCOTRAIL FRANCHISE

The last major unsold British Rail passenger franchise, Scotrail, has been awarded to the National Express Group by the franchising director, John O'Brian. ScotRail operates all local and commuter InterCity services over a 1,880-mile network and is responsible for sleeper services from Euston in London to Scotland. National Express fought off competition from Stagecoach and from a management buyout team. The sale could mean all 25 franchises will be in private hands by the election.
-- OUTPUT PRICES GIVE RATE HOPE TO CHANCELLOR

According to the Office for National Statistics, British output or factory gate prices rose only 0.2 percent in January, better than the 0.5 increase percent expected by the City. Chancellor Kenneth Clarke called the figures "staggeringly low" and said they have boosted his desire to avoid an increase in mortgage rates before the election. Jonathon Loynes, of HSBC Markets, said the figures were encouraging because January is the month when many manufacturers revise their list prices.
-- SE INQUIRY DID NOT TALK TO KEY CRAY DIRECTORS

A Stock Exchange investigation that led to Cray Electronics being cleared of issuing misleading statements to the market was completed without speaking to key members of senior management at Cray Communications. Former Cray Comms directors, who have alleged that group chief executive Jon Richards told them how Cray would cover up poor results from the data communications arm, were not interviewed. Former Cray Comms directors claim that the group's public statements bore little relation to the reality of the problems faced by its largest business.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SUIT WOULD WIPE OUT GKN PROFIT

One of Britain's biggest engineering companies, GKN, could see its 1996 profit wiped out by an American lawsuit. GKN could face a payout of more than 740 million dollars in a three-year case that was lost in December. The case was bought against Meineke Discount Muffler Shops, its US car exhaust business, by franchisees. Analysts say if the award is as high as expected, GKN's 500 million stg cash pile would be so severely depleted the group would not be able to make any planned acquisitions.
-- REBELS PROTEST AT A&L FLOAT'S 'DECEIT AND CONCEALMENT'

Alliance and Leicester has been accused of "deceit and concealment" by rebel investors who oppose its plans to list the building society on the stock market this April. Investors voiced their complaints at an official hearing of the Building Societies Commission, which must approve the conversion. Patrick Mountain, head of the investors' action group, said the society had behaved in an appalling manner towards some investors and he hoped the Bank of England would rule it unfit to become a bank.
-- MAJOR COURTS THE LATINS

Speaking at the Link into Latin America conference in London, Prime Minister John Major told politicians and business leaders that Britain and Latin America need to broaden their relationship beyond trade and investment, in an attempt to boost the UK's share of an expanding market. He advertised Britain's low social costs and flexible labour market as providing a "natural gateway to Europe". Major also urged strengthening joint efforts to combat drug trafficking, international crime, terrorism and tackling environmental problems.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BANK RAISES PRESSURE ON CLARKE WITH NEW DEMAND TO HIKE RATE

Tomorrow's Inflation Report from the Bank of England will contain a renewed demand for interest rates to rise. However, Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is expected to put politics first and avoid increasing borrowing and mortgage costs before the election. Treasury officials claim that their advice is being ignored by the chancellor and some, including the Bank of England, believe that the strength of the economy means base rates ought to rise to keep inflation on course for its target in the longer term. Recent weakness in some of the monthly economic statistics have given Clarke more room to manoeuvre.
-- AMERICAN AND BA PLAN CO-OPERATION STRATEGIES

British Airways is looking at ways to begin co-operation with American Airlines before regulatory hurdles in the US and Europe are overcome. Options being considered include sharing facilities at Heathrow and American's US hubs and joint marketing initiatives. The news comes as BA celebrates a decade in the private sector with record third-quarter profits and a special offer of 200 return Concorde tickets for 10 pounds stg.
-- SAFEWAY RAISES CARD WAR STAKES

Safeway has launched a new interest-paying plastic card account in partnership with Abbey National. Safeway will put its brand name on a card operated by an existing bank, similar to the concept used by Tesco. But Sainsbury's has confirmed it has received authorisation from the Bank of England to operate its planned joint venture with Bank of Scotland, thus creating its own bank. Safeway said it hoped its ABC bonus account card would attract new customers as well as buy the loyalty of existing ones.
